competitors.name: NestLens Orbit
competitors.pricing: ₹75,000 / ₹99,000 / ₹1,25,000 / ₹2,50,000 per year (Orbit Launch/Starter/Growth/Scale); Orbit PM ₹2,499/mo; Orbit OS ₹29,999/mo
competitors.scope: incubation OS: intake, screening, evaluation, cohorts, mentors, MOM transcription, grant ledger, compliance calendar
competitors.differentiator: Indian-language MOM transcription (Sarvam); NIDHI/DST-TBI/BIRAC/RKVY ledgers
competitors.weakness: No verifiable Indian customer; zero third-party reviews; internal pricing conflict

competitors.name: EcoSync
competitors.pricing: Login-gated; plans configured per deployment, monthly/weekly/yearly
competitors.scope: incubator CRM+ERP: programs, applications, weighted panel evaluation, office space, funding source-to-tranche, task boards
competitors.differentiator: India-first rails (INR/GST/TDS/UPI/IST); funding over-allocation blocked at entry; 12-status audit trail
competitors.weakness: VENDOR_CLAIM only - no third-party verification; no SOC 2 / ISO 27001 (self-disclosed); first customer is also the reference

competitors.name: Incubatee (SCIP)
competitors.pricing: Platform subscription ₹3,00,000/year (₹25,000/month)
competitors.scope: incubator platform; part of the scip.co group

competitors.weakness: Zero reviews; zero verifiable customers; no public feature detail

competitors.name: IncubatX
competitors.pricing: Foundation ₹10,000–15,000/mo · Accelerator ₹30,000–40,000/mo · Executive AI ₹50,000–60,000/mo · Media Kit add-on ₹15,000/mo
competitors.scope: incubator/accelerator OS: cohorts, funding, CSR, matchmaking, impact dashboard
competitors.differentiator: Published INR price list; top of the observed Indian envelope
competitors.weakness: Founded 2026, no track record; claims 240+ schemes but matches on sector/stage, not TRL; zero customers

competitors.name: Accubate
competitors.pricing: $149/user/month (aggregator); own site publishable-only
competitors.customers: NSRCEL, NASSCOM, TCS, Hero, KPMG, Accenture
competitors.scope: innovation programme management; Enterprise multi-site is genuinely the closest in the set
competitors.differentiator: Only competitor with a real review base (26 Capterra, 4.8); multi-site architecture
competitors.weakness: Per-user pricing collapses institutional ACV; documentation-poor; broken pricing page; scored 2/5 on AI by a competitor

competitors.name: Founderhood
competitors.pricing: Free · $199/mo · $649/mo · custom (no currency symbol published)
competitors.scope: incubator/accelerator CRM: applications, multi-phase evaluation, cohorts, mentors, live sessions, alumni
competitors.differentiator: Free tier with 15 startups/program; published 15% university/nonprofit discount
competitors.weakness: Publishing no currency symbol is a basic credibility failure; tiny company

competitors.name: VentureLink
competitors.pricing: Core $180/mo · Emails $30/mo · Events $30/mo · Jobs $15/mo · Onboarding $500 once
competitors.customers: ICUBE, University of Toronto (Ignacio Mongrell, Assistant Director)
competitors.scope: innovation ecosystem OS: intake, external judges, cohorts, mentors, desks, funding, flows automation, 760+ integrations
competitors.differentiator: The ONLY named university-institution reference found in the entire category; workflow automation at depth
competitors.weakness: Data residency is CANADA - fails Indian data-residency procurement; SOC 2 'in progress'; $225/mo still a real cost for a government TBI

competitors.name: incuTrack
competitors.pricing: $75/mo quarterly · $250/mo quarterly ($99/$325 monthly) · $595 one-time setup; add-ons $20–75/mo
competitors.scope: incubator CRM: prospects, companies, milestones, economic impact, room inventory, invoicing
competitors.differentiator: 20+ years of tenure; long review history
competitors.weakness: Recent reviewers call it 'quite outdated'; no Indian customers; English/US institutional assumptions

competitors.name: RiserNest
competitors.pricing: €399/mo (≤30 teams) · €799/mo (30–100) · €1,500/mo (100+), ex-VAT; per-user tiers €40/70/120 also shown
competitors.scope: incubator/accelerator OS: onboarding, stages, milestones, mentor visibility, community app, white-label
competitors.differentiator: White-label available; claims program-size pricing not per-seat
competitors.weakness: 4 employees; CONTRADICTS itself - says 'No per-seat pricing' while displaying per-user tiers; no security certification

competitors.name: Gohorto
competitors.pricing: US$4,200/year flat (Capterra); Starter/Professional/Enterprise pilot tiers on own site
competitors.scope: full incubation lifecycle: intake, AI mentor matching, milestones, graduation, analytics
competitors.differentiator: Addresses the multi-programme complexity Indian institutions actually have
competitors.weakness: 3 reviews, one vendor-referred; no named customer; flat annual price only

competitors.name: Univation (Incubators Platform)
competitors.pricing: FREE for universities and nonprofits (+ $1,000 Google Ads credit)
competitors.scope: incubator/accelerator programme management - the same job as StartupHub
competitors.differentiator: Free for exactly the buyer StartupHub targets
competitors.weakness: Tiny company; free tier caps at 15 startups/program

competitors.name: Innoloft / LoftOS
competitors.pricing: Free – $849/month
competitors.scope: no-code portal builder with an accelerator template
competitors.differentiator: THE DIY THREAT - a university IT team can build its own
competitors.weakness: Not purpose-built; heavy implementation; no incubation domain model

competitors.name: AcceleratorApp
competitors.pricing: Core quote-only; funding module $549–899/month
competitors.customers: Yale, MIT Design X, Max Planck (no Indian institution)
competitors.scope: accelerator management with tranche disbursement and capital calls
competitors.differentiator: Best academic logos in the category; capital-call machinery
competitors.weakness: Zero Indian presence; quote-gated core; no verified reviews

competitors.name: IdeaScale
competitors.pricing: $4,999 per feature per year (aggregator); enterprise custom
competitors.customers: White House, NASA, McKinsey, IKEA, Ford, Target, Pfizer
competitors.scope: enterprise idea/innovation management, crowdsourcing, gamification, prioritisation
competitors.differentiator: Largest installed base in enterprise innovation; sold to government and academia
competitors.weakness: Corporate intrapreneurial; assumes employee base, SSO, IT dept; no Indian institution

competitors.name: Envisio
competitors.pricing: CONFLICT: GetApp USD 400/yr vs SelectHub USD 20,000/yr; observed contract USD 19,500/yr + USD 8,775 setup
competitors.customers: City of La Mesa, CA (council resolution, USD 19,500/yr)
competitors.scope: public-sector strategy + performance dashboards, unlimited user licences
competitors.differentiator: Serves ONLY public sector, nonprofit and education - closest buyer match outside India
competitors.weakness: Not a startup platform; no India presence; 50x aggregator conflict unresolved

competitors.name: Throttle
competitors.pricing: ¥980 / ¥1,980 / ¥2,980 / ¥3,980 per user per month, ex-tax
competitors.scope: innovation management: ideation, programme operations, incubator run
competitors.differentiator: #1 market share in Japan; per-user tiers with volume discounts
competitors.weakness: Japan-only market assumptions; no India presence

competitors.name: Wazoku
competitors.pricing: Total Innovation License - $15,000 per Admin/year, unlimited end users
competitors.scope: innovation OS + Innocentive marketplace (1M members), xV value metric, ecosystem management
competitors.differentiator: Unlimited end users at a per-admin price - the correct shape for institutions
competitors.weakness: Priced at enterprise scale; no India presence; incumbent-ecosystem assumptions

competitors.name: Incu (Sweden)
competitors.pricing: 790 kr/user/month
competitors.scope: innovation management with maturity levels and a patent data field
competitors.differentiator: THE ONLY competitor anywhere with any patent awareness - as a data field, not a workflow
competitors.weakness: A data field is not an IP workflow; no India presence

competitors.name: Dealum
competitors.pricing: Essentials $119/mo · Advance $289/mo · Scale $479/mo (annual); higher monthly
competitors.scope: accelerator lifecycle: application to graduation to first round and exit
competitors.differentiator: Deal-room depth for investor-facing workflow
competitors.weakness: No India presence; no institutional/mandate features

competitors.name: FIKR
competitors.pricing: Free · Growth €149/mo · Scale €399/mo
competitors.scope: accelerator OS: applications, AI screening, cohorts, mentor matching, demo day, analytics
competitors.differentiator: Full white-label portal on Scale; genuine free tier
competitors.weakness: Africa-first assumptions; no India presence

competitors.name: FosiaHub
competitors.pricing: Hub $299/mo · Accelerator $799/mo · free 90-day pilot for institutions
competitors.scope: accelerator/development-agency programmes: AI scoring, cohorts, credits, donor reporting
competitors.differentiator: Donor/funder reporting and credits distribution - funder-shaped, not institution-shaped
competitors.weakness: Africa-first; no India presence

competitors.name: European Startup Hub
competitors.pricing: Institutional licence from €15,000/yr · Regional from €50,000/yr · Portal Cloud from €2,500 · Accelerator infrastructure from €12,000
competitors.scope: operating layer for university hubs and regional innovation networks
competitors.differentiator: THE ONLY institutional-licence model found - per licence, not per seat
competitors.weakness: Very high price point; Europe public-sector shaped; no India presence

competitors.name: Catalyzer
competitors.pricing: Free version available; paid tiers request-demo
competitors.scope: cohort management, CRM, intake, session tracking, longitudinal impact surveys
competitors.differentiator: SOC 2 and WCAG 2.1 AA certified - the only certified competitor found
competitors.weakness: US federal/state funding-report framing; no India presence

competitors.name: Wellspring for Tech Transfer
competitors.pricing: Custom quote
competitors.scope: inventions, patents, licences, startups, spin-outs; deadline management; venture programmes
competitors.differentiator: Full patent deadline management - the TTO-side half of GAP-01
competitors.weakness: Quote-only; university research offices, not incubators; no India presence

competitors.name: Helikon Labs
competitors.pricing: Free · Team $19/seat/month (5–25 seats) · Institutional from 25 seats (scoped)
competitors.scope: research partnership lifecycle: researchers, patents, CPC codes, NDA/IRB/contract compliance dates, TTO pipeline
competitors.differentiator: Starts tracking at DISCLOSURE - before any system of record sees it
competitors.weakness: Per-seat pricing; no India presence; research-office shaped

competitors.name: Commercify
competitors.pricing: University/research institution from $30,000/yr · Corporate innovation from $75,000/yr (planned GA; 6 design partners)
competitors.scope: tech transfer offices and corporate R&D: spin-outs, licensing targets, cap-table modelling
competitors.differentiator: Commercialisation-outcome framing, not process framing
competitors.weakness: Pre-GA; only 6 design partner slots; very high price; no India presence

competitors.name: SINT.OTRI
competitors.pricing: Pilot €0 (6 months) · Year 1 €14,000 + VAT · Year 2+ €55,000/yr
competitors.scope: university patent portfolio with annuity calendar, art.83 LOSU contracts, spin-offs, invention declarations
competitors.differentiator: Deliberately priced below the Spanish minor-contract threshold to enable direct award
competitors.weakness: Spanish public-law specific (LOSU art.83); no India presence

competitors.name: Elsevier Pure
competitors.pricing: UK G-Cloud list £19,406–£58,504/yr + £32,250 onboarding
competitors.scope: research outputs, funding, affiliations, impact - the research management benchmark
competitors.differentiator: The hardest price benchmark in the study; institutional-grade trust
competitors.weakness: Manages RESEARCH OUTPUTS, not startups; no India-specific module; very expensive

ecosystem.name: Startup India Hub
ecosystem.gives: 50,000+ startup directory; investors, mentors, incubators, accelerators; 30+ government bodies registered; free tools, templates, courses, challenges; Innovation Challenges with cash grants
ecosystem.takes_back: **NOTHING BACK TO INSTITUTIONS.** No IIC activity, no ARIIA/NIRF evidence, no TRL. This is the single most important line in this phase.
ecosystem.overlap: DIRECT on networking, directory, mentors, incubators. ZERO on institutional innovation compliance.

ecosystem.name: BHASKAR
ecosystem.gives: Bharat Startup Knowledge Access Registry; personas Mentor, Enabler, Explorer, Startup Founder, Individual Investor, Traditional Business Owner; industry alliances by sector/tech/geography
ecosystem.takes: a completed profile before you become visible and searchable
ecosystem.takes_back: **NOTHING BACK TO INSTITUTIONS.** Identity layer, not an innovation record.
ecosystem.overlap: Identity and discovery. No institutional compliance overlap at all.
ecosystem.note: Registration now redirects through BHASKAR before DPIIT recognition runs in parallel.

ecosystem.name: MAARG
ecosystem.gives: AI mentor-startup matching at scale; interaction tracking for impact; video calls; mentor recognition; custom programmes by enablers; feedback and grievance mechanism
ecosystem.takes_back: **NOTHING BACK TO INSTITUTIONS.** Mentorship hours are not logged against any scheme's utilisation requirement.
ecosystem.overlap: DIRECT on mentor matching. This is the closest government analogue to StartupHub's mentor module.
ecosystem.note: GAP-07 (NDA-tiered mentor visibility) is NOT solved here either.

ecosystem.name: Startup India Investor Connect
ecosystem.gives: dedicated platform connecting startups to investors by sector, function, stage, geography, background
ecosystem.note: Launched at the 6th NSAC meeting, 11 March 2023.

ecosystem.name: IIC Portal
ecosystem.gives: Institution's Innovation Council registration; star rating 1–5; Performance Card; 16+ activities/year each a full evidence submission
ecosystem.takes: 16+ evidence submissions per year, maintained by hand
ecosystem.takes_back: Nothing - this IS the record. But it returns nothing machine-readable.
ecosystem.overlap: **TOTAL, AND MANDATORY.** No institution can opt out. This is the demand driver.

ecosystem.name: YUKTI-NIR
ecosystem.gives: TRL banding (Idea/PoC 1–4, Innovation/Prototype 5–9, Business/Startup); institute-side verification with Recommended/Not-Recommended gating; auto-flows to ARIIA
ecosystem.takes_back: Improved ARIIA Section 4 ranking - a budget line that already exists.
ecosystem.note: GOV-023/024. The reason TRL is non-optional (GAP-02).

ecosystem.name: NIRF Innovation
ecosystem.gives: Ranking; 5 marks hinge on one countable (startups recognised)
ecosystem.note: GOV-028. Phase 3A measured the operational cost: 32/354 startups lose identity (9%).

ecosystem.name: ARIIA
ecosystem.gives: Ranking; incumbent performance data; 100+ indicators across 5 categories
ecosystem.note: GOV-032. Demands 'Patent Application No' and 'Year of Patent Application' - the mandate behind GAP-01.

ecosystem.name: AISHE
ecosystem.gives: National registry; the statistical frame behind every count in this study
ecosystem.overlap: Indirect - it defines the market, not the workflow.
ecosystem.note: 58,643 registered HEIs - the super-bound from Phase 7.

ecosystem.name: State Startup Portals
ecosystem.gives: State Startup Ranking (SRF) results; policy schemes; state nodal teams
ecosystem.overlap: Segment G9 - sized separately in Phase 7 on the PRIOR tier.
ecosystem.note: Phase 6: 34 states ranked, 8 fell tiers, 0 Emerging-tier reports obtainable.

indirect.name: Excel / Google Sheets
indirect.why_it_wins: Free, universal, no procurement. Every institution already has it.
indirect.what_it_cannot_do: No permissions, no audit trail, no relational integrity, no workflow, manual consolidation across departments.
indirect.evidence: PHASE 4 corpus - the IIC annual report is hand-assembled from spreadsheets (P-A08)

indirect.name: WhatsApp + Google Drive
indirect.why_it_wins: It is the operational database. IISc's own IIC page links students to a WhatsApp group.
indirect.what_it_cannot_do: No structure, no permissions, no audit trail, no reporting.

indirect.name: Notion / Superhuman Docs
indirect.why_it_wins: Flexible, cheap at small team size, attractive UI that staff already want to use.
indirect.what_it_cannot_do: Audit logs gated behind Enterprise; no retroactive history; no offline; no Indian compliance.

indirect.name: Airtable
indirect.why_it_wins: The default 'build it ourselves' database. RiserNest and VentureLink both position against it by name.
indirect.what_it_cannot_do: No institutional domain model; audit history limited; Indian data residency uncertain.

indirect.name: CRM (Zoho / Freshworks / Freshsales)
indirect.why_it_wins: Cheap, ubiquitous, and the incumbent IIC coordinators already know.
indirect.what_it_cannot_do: Models PIPELINE, not incubation. No TRL, no IPR, no scheme mapping. Per-user pricing collapses institutional ACV (Phase 8).

indirect.name: Project management (Trello / ClickUp / Monday / Asana)
indirect.why_it_wins: Task tracking is the visible symptom; teams adopt it before anything else.
indirect.what_it_cannot_do: No domain model, no intake workflow, no IPR. Audit logs enterprise-only.

indirect.name: Campus ERP (Fedena, EduZenAI, Campusify)
indirect.why_it_wins: The institution already owns one and pays for it regardless. Fedena sells a broader product for ₹1,00,000 flat.
indirect.what_it_cannot_do: **Zero Indian campus ERP vendors have a startup-incubation module.** They stop at admissions, fees and exams.
indirect.evidence: Phase 8 comparables; Phase 9 campus ERP row

indirect.name: Email + Word/Excel
indirect.why_it_wins: Always works, always available, needs no committee.
indirect.what_it_cannot_do: No calculation, no lineage, binary re-entry, month-end blackout.

global_subcategories.tech_transfer: Tech transfer / IP management platforms (added by Phase 9)

positioning_gaps.title: IPR / patent portfolio management
positioning_gaps.verdict: NARROWED BY PHASE 9 - was 'zero competitors have an IPR module'
positioning_gaps.phase0_claim: Zero of 11 competitors have an IPR module.
positioning_gaps.falsified_by: Wellspring for Tech Transfer, Helikon Labs, Commercify and SINT.OTRI all implement invention disclosure, patent status/deadline, licensing and spin-out workflow. Four dedicated tech-transfer platforms exist.
positioning_gaps.surviving_claim: Dedicated IP/tech-transfer platforms EXIST but are not JOINED TO INCUBATION PROGRAMME MANAGEMENT, and none has Indian data residency. Incu (Sweden) has a patent field but not a workflow.
positioning_gaps.nearest: Wellspring, Helikon Labs, Commercify, SINT.OTRI (TTO side); Incu (Sweden, field)
positioning_gaps.why_india: ARIIA demands 'Patent Application No'; IIC registers IPR/TTO Centre by floor area with no patent field; MeitY mandates IP due diligence; HEI filings +119% in two years

positioning_gaps.title: TRL as a first-class, reportable object
positioning_gaps.verdict: UNCHANGED - not touched by Phase 9 research
positioning_gaps.phase0_claim: Every platform tracks 'stage' as free text. Nobody models TRL.
positioning_gaps.falsified_by: None found. Incu (Sweden) has maturity levels but no funding-scheme mapping.
positioning_gaps.surviving_claim: Every platform tracks 'stage' as free text. Nobody models TRL AND maps it to eligible Indian funding schemes.
positioning_gaps.why_india: YUKTI-NIR bands on TRL 1–9; ARIIA asks for 'Stage of Innovation (TRL Stage)'; BIRAC/NIDHI/TIDE tranches tied to TRL progression

positioning_gaps.title: YUKTI-NIR / IIC / ARIIA submission workflow
positioning_gaps.verdict: UNCHANGED - not touched by Phase 9 research
positioning_gaps.phase0_claim: Highest-value, most-defensible feature in the category - and completely open.
positioning_gaps.falsified_by: None. No competitor, Indian or global, targets Indian government mandates.
positioning_gaps.surviving_claim: Zero of 29 competitors. Highest-value and most-defensible gap in the category.
positioning_gaps.why_india: Government mandate across three separate systems; verified YUKTI-NIR entries improve ARIIA ranking

positioning_gaps.title: Unified mandate-spanning reporting
positioning_gaps.verdict: WEAKENED - Accubate Enterprise now has a real claim
positioning_gaps.phase0_claim: Nobody reports the whole institutional innovation portfolio at once.
positioning_gaps.falsified_by: Accubate Enterprise multi-site is genuinely the closest structure.
positioning_gaps.surviving_claim: Accubate has multi-site structure but no Indian mandate spans.
positioning_gaps.why_india: One institution files to ARIIA, NIRF, IIC, AICTE/NBA/NAAC, DST/NIDHI/BIRAC/TIDE, CSR, AIC, Governing Body, DPIIT

positioning_gaps.title: Government-grant disbursement ledger traced to a receipt
positioning_gaps.verdict: STRENGTHENED - Phase 9 found a fourth holder
positioning_gaps.phase0_claim: Cover with scheme-matching, not a general ledger.
positioning_gaps.falsified_by: VentureLink adds grants/competitions tracked per team, raising holders to 4.
positioning_gaps.surviving_claim: Everyone has a general ledger; nobody scheme-matches to Indian eligibility.
positioning_gaps.why_india: BIRAC 5% royalty until cumulative repayment; unspent balance reversion is an audit failure

positioning_gaps.title: Faculty, Innovation Ambassadors and the non-startup innovator
positioning_gaps.verdict: NARROWED - tech-transfer platforms do model faculty
positioning_gaps.phase0_claim: Completely unoccupied, and upstream of the whole funnel.
positioning_gaps.falsified_by: Wellspring, Helikon Labs and Commercify all centre the FACULTY/researcher as the primary entity - the opposite of StartupHub's startup-first model.
positioning_gaps.surviving_claim: Faculty are first-class in TECH-TRANSFER platforms but absent from every INCUBATION platform, which all build from 'startup application'.
positioning_gaps.nearest: Wellspring, Helikon Labs (faculty entity, no incubation)
positioning_gaps.why_india: MIC trained 60,000+ faculty as Innovation Ambassadors; NIDHI-PRAYAS requires an institutional NOC from employed applicants

positioning_gaps.title: Mentor logistics at scale - NDA-tiered visibility
positioning_gaps.verdict: WEAKENED BY ECOSYSTEM - MAARG is a government actor here
positioning_gaps.phase0_claim: A real institutional fear that nobody has solved.
positioning_gaps.falsified_by: MAARG (Startup India) does AI mentor matching at national scale, though without NDA tiers.
positioning_gaps.surviving_claim: MAARG matches mentors but does not tier visibility by NDA and does not log hours against scheme utilisation. The NDA gap itself survives.
positioning_gaps.why_india: A single NDA leakage could void an IPR claim; AICTE YUKTI-NIR has NDA templates

positioning_gaps.title: AI that is auditable instead of just advertised
positioning_gaps.verdict: WEAKENED - AI adoption is now broad
positioning_gaps.phase0_claim: Nothing in the category offers defensible AI.
positioning_gaps.falsified_by: FIKR (10-pillar AI pitch scoring), Dealum (AI assistant credits), IdeaScale (AI assistance), VentureLink (audit log on every score change), IncubatX, EcoSync.
positioning_gaps.surviving_claim: AI is now widespread, but audit trails are the differentiator: VentureLink logs every score change with actor and reason, and EcoSync refuses AI scoring outright.
positioning_gaps.nearest: VentureLink (score-change audit log), EcoSync (counter-position on AI scoring)
positioning_gaps.why_india: AI that cannot produce a citation trail is worse than no AI for an auditable committee process

positioning_gaps.title: Unincorporated pre-incubation state
positioning_gaps.verdict: UNCHANGED - no competitor found to model it
positioning_gaps.phase0_claim: The biggest structural hole in every platform.
positioning_gaps.falsified_by: None found. Every platform assumes a registered entity.
positioning_gaps.surviving_claim: Every platform assumes a registered entity; the university funnel is mostly before incorporation.
positioning_gaps.nearest: Incubatee - one line item on the pricing table
positioning_gaps.why_india: DPIIT recognition, GST and Udyam gate every scheme; SIH had 139,844 teams registered

positioning_gaps.title: Guaranteed migration off forms/spreadsheets/WhatsApp
positioning_gaps.verdict: WEAKENED - more vendors now claim it
positioning_gaps.falsified_by: VentureLink (data import in onboarding), Helikon Labs (start free), Phosphor-free onboarding in others.
positioning_gaps.surviving_claim: Still the #1 real blocker in an Indian institutional sale; more vendors claim it than actually do it.
positioning_gaps.why_india: Migration is manual, unpaid work the BUYER must do

positioning_gaps.title: Departments and multi-campus sub-tenancy
positioning_gaps.verdict: WEAKENED - more vendors now claim multi-site
positioning_gaps.falsified_by: IdeaScale, Wazoku, Helikon Labs, ESH and Elsevier Pure all now claim multi-site or departmental structure.
positioning_gaps.surviving_claim: Multi-site is becoming table stakes; sub-tenant-per-DEPARTMENT with departmental P&L and SPV-vs-department IP ownership is still absent.
positioning_gaps.why_india: Departments each hold their own IIC coordinator, budget and mentor panel

positioning_gaps.title: Deployment model an Indian university can actually buy
positioning_gaps.phase0_claim: Nobody packages on-premise/Indian data residency at an affordable price.
positioning_gaps.falsified_by: None. EcoSync is INR-native but cloud; VentureLink is Canada-resident; Catalyzer is certified but US.
positioning_gaps.surviving_claim: Still unoccupied. Note Phase 8: Fedena sells a FULL ERP at ₹1,00,000 flat, so the market exists - StartupHub must simply match that shape.
positioning_gaps.why_india: Only Incubatee, IncubatX and Orbit publish an India price list

positioning_gaps.title: A verifiable Indian reference institution
positioning_gaps.phase0_claim: No competitor can prove a large Indian institution runs on their software.
positioning_gaps.falsified_by: EcoSync names TBI-KIET (KIET Group of Institutions); Accubate names NSRCOM and NASSCOM; VentureLink publishes a NAMED_REFERENCE from ICUBE at the University of Toronto, which is a university incubator but NOT Indian.
positioning_gaps.surviving_claim: No competitor demonstrates a LARGE INDIAN UNIVERSITY deployment with named referees and third-party verification. The best evidence in the category is a VENDOR_CLAIM (EcoSync) and a NAMED_REFERENCE at a non-Indian university.
positioning_gaps.nearest: EcoSync (TBI-KIET, vendor-claimed); VentureLink (ICUBE Toronto, named reference)
positioning_gaps.why_india: Named Indian university case study with referees is still worth more than any feature

revised_claims.phase0_claim: No competitor can prove a large Indian institution runs on their software.
revised_claims.falsified_by: EcoSync (TBI-KIET); Accubate (NSRCOM, NASSCOM); VentureLink (ICUBE, Univ. of Toronto)
revised_claims.correction: Narrowed to: no competitor demonstrates a LARGE INDIAN UNIVERSITY deployment with named referees and third-party verification.

revised_claims.phase0_claim: Exactly zero competitors have an IPR module.

regulatory_signals.change: Startup recognition turnover threshold revised from ₹100 crore to ₹200 crore.
